deliverables: Audit and oversight through Intersect and technically capable third-party reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls
Use of TRSC and PSSC treasury management smart contracts for fund administration
request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v
request.what: Withdraw treasury funds for Mithril Protocol continuous development with Intersect budget administration.

claims.claim: Mithril is presented as solving the cost and complexity of securely accessing and verifying Cardano blockchain state by using stake-based threshold multi-signatures to certify Cardano state trustlessly.
The proposal states that faster sync times enabled by Mithril lower onboarding friction and unlock tooling for exchanges, wallets, and monitoring.
The proposal states that Mithril enables community-built bridges, light wallets, full wallets, light clients, and monitoring tools around Cardano.

The proposal says it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides references to the vote, documentation, audited results, and audit report.
The proposal asserts that the requested amount does not, at time of submission, breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 and links to the NCL governance action.
The budget summary allocates 3,699,440 ada to Mithril Protocol Continuous Development and 110,983 ada to an Intersect Budget Administration fee, totaling 3,810,423 ada.

The proposal states that audit, oversight, reporting obligations, and milestone-based disbursement controls are included through Intersect, an administration fee, and technically capable third-party oversight.
The proposal states that Teragone has not previously received direct Cardano treasury or community governance funding, while IOG has funded its Mithril work to date.

The proposal identifies deployed 2026 treasury management smart contract addresses, permission thresholds, an oversight committee, supporting documentation, audits, a GitHub repository, and a public dashboard for tracking funds.

The proposal does not state specific development milestones, acceptance criteria, delivery dates, or a detailed cost basis for the 3,699,440 ada continuous development work package in the anchor text.

summary: The proposal requests 3,810,423 ada for Mithril Protocol continuous development and Intersect administration, with governance-process, NCL, smart-contract, audit, and dashboard references, but the anchor text lacks detailed milestones, acceptance criteria, delivery dates, and cost basis for the main work package.
